data.title: Tesla AI5 supply constraints could explain decision to stick with AI4: Report
data.description:
Tesla’s recent changes to its artificial intelligence (AI) hardware come as a new report points to potential AI5 chip supply constraints as another possible factor behind why its cars will continue using AI4.

According to a report from Commercial Times citing supply chain sources, Tesla’s chip design partner Global Unichip Corp. (GUC) is facing limited access to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s (TSMC) 3-nanometre manufacturing capacity.

While GUC is expected to receive a substantially larger allocation in 2027, priority will reportedly be given to data centre chip orders from Google and Microsoft.

The remaining capacity may not be enough to support Tesla’s annual vehicle production, with the report saying widespread deployment of AI5 in cars may have to wait until 2028.

Musk said AI4 is enough for superhuman driving

On Sunday, CEO Elon Musk said Tesla would continue using AI4 in its cars, explaining that the existing hardware was already powerful enough to achieve driving capabilities beyond those of humans.

“It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”

Rising memory costs force hardware changes

Musk also said that rising memory and storage prices have doubled the cost of AI4, prompting Tesla to scale back the memory planned for AI4.5.

“RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints.”

Tesla made similar changes to AI5 in October, initially cutting its RAM allocation in half to 72GB to help get enough volume for Optimus production, before settling on 96GB.

Optimus takes priority over Tesla vehicles

While Musk has described AI5 as offering roughly 12 times more computing power than AI4, the report suggests limited chip availability could be another factor behind Tesla’s decision to keep it out of cars.

During Tesla’s October 21, 2026, earnings call, Musk said the company planned to integrate AI5 into Optimus around April 2027, if things go according to plan.

data.title: The 10 cheapest EVs to buy before Canada’s federal rebate drops by $1,000
data.description:
Canadians looking to buy a new electric vehicle (EV) have just over a month left at the current $5,000 Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP) rebate, before the federal incentive drops by $1,000.

According to Transport Canada, the maximum incentive for a fully electric vehicle purchase, or a lease of at least 48 months, will be reduced to $4,000 as of January 1, 2027. However, the amount buyers receive is determined by when their dealership submits the eligibility assessment, not when they purchase or take delivery of their vehicle.

There are currently several eligible EVs with a base manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) below $40,000, with the federal incentive bringing Canada’s cheapest electric car below $30,000 before freight, fees and taxes.

The 10 cheapest electric vehicles in Canada

Here are the 10 cheapest new fully electric vehicles eligible for the federal rebate in Canada, ranked by their base MSRP as of November 27, 2026.

  1. 2027 Nissan Leaf S: $34,998 ($29,998 after EVAP)
  2. 2027 Kia EV3 Light FWD: $36,995 ($31,995 after EVAP)
  3. 2026 Kia EV4 Light FWD: $38,995 ($33,995 after EVAP)
  4. 2026 Fiat 500e Pop: $39,995 ($34,995 after EVAP)
  5. 2027 Chevrolet Bolt LT: $39,999 ($34,999 after EVAP)
  6. 2027 Subaru Uncharted FWD: $40,995 ($35,995 after EVAP)
  7. 2027 Hyundai Kona Electric Preferred: $43,999 ($38,999 after EVAP)
  8. 2027 Toyota C-HR SE FWD: $44,895 ($39,895 after EVAP)
  9. 2027 Toyota bZ XLE FWD: $45,985 ($40,985 after EVAP)
  10. 2026 Ford Mustang Mach-E Select RWD Standard Range: $46,995 ($41,995 after EVAP)

The 2027 Nissan Leaf S remains Canada’s cheapest new EV, coming in nearly $2,000 below the Kia EV3. Buyers interested in the Kia EV4 can also save a little more by opting for the 2026 model, with the equivalent 2027 Light FWD trim priced $600 higher at $39,595.

Understanding the $50,000 EV rebate price limit

It is worth noting that the prices listed above do not include freight and pre-delivery inspection (PDI) charges, dealer fees or taxes, all of which will increase the amount buyers ultimately pay.

For example, the Nissan Leaf S has a listed selling price of $37,966 once freight, PDI and other applicable fees are included, bringing it down to $32,966 after the federal rebate, before taxes.

Buyers should also keep in mind that sales taxes are calculated on the full price of the vehicle, including freight and PDI, before government rebates are applied. While the $5,000 federal rebate reduces the amount buyers ultimately pay, it does not reduce the amount of sales tax they owe.

Buyers also need to pay attention to EVAP’s $50,000 final transaction value limit. While freight and PDI are excluded from that calculation, optional equipment, premium paint colours and dealer fees count towards the limit.

This is particularly important for vehicles towards the bottom of the list, where adding a few options or moving up to a more expensive trim could make the vehicle ineligible for the entire federal rebate.

How to secure the full $5,000 EV rebate before 2027

Canadians who cannot take delivery of their new EV before the end of December can still receive the full $5,000 incentive in 2027, provided their dealership submits the eligibility assessment before the end of this year.

In its EVAP questions and answers, Transport Canada gives the example of a buyer receiving pre-approval on December 2, 2026, and taking delivery on February 21, 2027, who would still qualify for the $5,000 rebate.

Conversely, someone taking delivery on November 26, 2026, whose dealership does not submit the eligibility assessment until January 7, 2027, would only qualify for the reduced $4,000 incentive.

Eligibility assessments are valid for 90 days, with dealerships having until December 31, 2026, to submit them at the current incentive amount.

What about Tesla?

While Tesla does not have a vehicle among the 10 cheapest EVs in Canada, the Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD) is eligible for the federal rebate. With a base MSRP of $49,990, the electric SUV comes down to $44,990 after the current $5,000 incentive.

However, with a base price sitting just $10 below EVAP’s $50,000 limit, buyers need to be careful when selecting paid options, such as upgraded paint colours, wheels or interior finishes.

The bigger issue for Tesla buyers, though, is the long wait for delivery. Earlier this month Tesla pushed back Model Y delivery estimates in Canada, with new orders showing estimated delivery windows between March and May 2027.

With EVAP pre-approvals only valid for 90 days, many customers ordering a Model Y today could miss out on the full $5,000 rebate. Buyers hoping to secure the higher incentive may have better luck finding an eligible Model Y in Tesla’s existing inventory.

Meanwhile, Tesla’s Model 3 remains ineligible for the federal rebate because it is manufactured in China, unlike the Canadian Model Y, which is imported from Giga Berlin in Germany.

Disclaimer: All prices listed in this article are based on manufacturer pricing available at the time of publication and are subject to change. Actual selling prices, vehicle availability, dealer fees and rebate eligibility may vary. Buyers should always check with their local dealership to confirm the latest pricing and eligibility for government incentives before making a purchase.

data.title: Tesla opens its first 500 kW V4 Supercharger in South Korea
data.description:
Tesla has opened its first 500 kW Supercharger in South Korea, expanding its rollout of true V4 charging stations with a new location along one of the country’s major highways.

In an announcement on Friday, Tesla Korea confirmed the opening of 16 stalls at the Deokpyeong Natural Rest Area along the Yeongdong Expressway.

Interestingly, the new station is split between two locations, with eight stalls serving drivers travelling towards Incheon and another eight serving those heading towards Gangneung, allowing owners to charge without having to cross the highway.

This is a similar setup to the Superchargers in Severn, Ontario, where Tesla installed charging posts on either side of Hwy 11.

Tesla brings 500 kW charging to South Korea

Unlike earlier V4 Superchargers that paired the newer charging posts with older V3 cabinets, the South Korean location features both V4 posts and V4 cabinets, supporting charging speeds of up to 500 kW.

The new cabinets support vehicle architectures ranging from 400V to 1,000V, allowing electric vehicles (EVs) built on 800V platforms to take advantage of higher charging speeds, depending on their individual charging capabilities.

Built-in Magic Dock for charging other EVs

Tesla has also equipped the stalls with its built-in Magic Dock adapters, allowing owners of non-Tesla EVs equipped with CCS1 charging ports to use the station without bringing their own adapter. The longer charging cables on the V4 posts also make it easier to accommodate vehicles with different charge port locations.

The opening comes just two days after General Motors announced an agreement to adopt Tesla’s North American Charging Standard (NACS) in South Korea, further expanding Tesla’s charging presence in the country.

Tesla is also preparing to bring its 500 kW charging technology to more locations in Canada, with construction underway on Quebec’s first true V4 Supercharger in Terrebonne.

data.title: Here’s What Tesla’s New Battery Preconditioning Controls Look Like [2026.44.3.1]
data.description:
Tesla’s new Manual Battery Preconditioning feature is now reaching owners with software update 2026.44.3.1. The update has so far been rolling out primarily to vehicles in Europe, and one owner has shared a first look at the new feature, showing how the new controls work in both the Tesla mobile app and the vehicle’s touchscreen.

The new controls are integrated directly into the existing Charging menu, with Tesla adding a “Precondition for Fast Charging” button immediately below the option to open the charge port.

Manual Battery Preconditioning in the Tesla App

Once activated, a yellow heating icon appears alongside a notification at the top of the Charging screen, informing owners that battery preconditioning is underway.

“Battery preconditioning in progress,” the notification reads, followed by “Heating pack to optimize fast charging performance.”

The activation button also changes to “Stop Preconditioning,” allowing owners to manually end the process at any time. Tesla has included a link underneath the controls where owners can learn more about battery preconditioning.

In-Car Battery Preconditioning Controls

The vehicle’s touchscreen offers a nearly identical layout, but with one additional visual element. When preconditioning is active, an animated-style progress indicator appears beneath the notification, providing a visual indication that the battery is being heated.

The addition of manual controls removes the need to enter a fast charging destination into Tesla’s navigation system to trigger battery preconditioning.

As detailed in the release notes, Tesla recommends activating the feature about an hour before a planned fast charging session. Once the battery reaches its optimal temperature, the vehicle will maintain it for 30 minutes.

Accessing the new controls remotely requires Tesla mobile app version 4.63.0, which was released ahead of the vehicle software update.

Why Battery Preconditioning Matters

Manual Battery Preconditioning allows Tesla owners to heat their vehicle’s battery to its optimal fast charging temperature without having to navigate to a charging station. The feature is particularly useful during colder weather, when a cold battery can significantly limit charging speeds.

By starting the process before leaving home or work, owners can arrive at a fast charger with a battery ready to accept higher charging rates, reducing the time spent plugged in.

data.title: Tesla seeks regulatory approval to acquire German machine-tool maker EMAG
data.description:
Tesla has taken the next step in its plans to acquire German machine-tool manufacturer EMAG, filing for regulatory approval with Germany’s Federal Cartel Office.

The proposed acquisition appeared on the competition regulator’s list of ongoing proceedings on Friday, providing the first official indication that Tesla is moving forward with a deal involving the German company, according to Handelsblatt.

Tesla moves forward with EMAG acquisition

Earlier this week, we reported that Tesla was preparing to acquire a stake in EMAG, with around 220 employees expected to move over to the automaker. The two companies have reportedly been working together for some time on technology related to humanoid robots.

Tesla has also established a new subsidiary called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE, registering its business address at EMAG’s headquarters in Salach. The new company is headed by Maximilian Stromberger, who oversees Tesla’s sales and vehicle deliveries in Germany.

Supporting Tesla’s Optimus production plans

EMAG specializes in machinery used to mass-produce precision metal components. Among its offerings are manufacturing systems for flexsplines, wave generators and planetary gears, all of which are used in the actuators that control the movement of humanoid robots.

The proposed acquisition comes as Tesla ramps up production of its Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, with the company aiming to reach a production rate of 20,000 robots per week in about a year. Tesla is also building a dedicated Optimus factory on the Giga Texas campus.

It would also mark another expansion of Tesla’s manufacturing operations in Germany, following its acquisition of assets and workforce from insolvent German automation supplier Manz AG.

EMAG faces financial struggles

EMAG has been struggling financially amid weak demand in the machine-tool industry. The company recorded a loss of €42 million (C$65.5 million) on revenue of €496 million (C$773 million) in 2024.

In November 2025, EMAG announced plans to cut 455 jobs across Germany, including around 300 at its headquarters in Salach.

data.title: Prevost unveils its first electric highway coach, the H3-45 Electric
data.description:
Canadian motorcoach manufacturer Prevost has unveiled the H3-45 Electric, its first fully electric highway coach, with up to 250 miles (400 km) of range and seating for up to 52 passengers.

Prevost, which is part of the Volvo Group, announced the North American launch of the new coach on Thursday at its manufacturing facility in Sainte-Claire, Quebec.

The H3-45 Electric has a 540 kWh battery system, with 459 kWh usable, spread across six Volvo Cube 2 packs.

Power comes from two Volvo electric motors delivering a rated output of 450 kW (600 hp), paired with an automated eight-speed transmission and adjustable regenerative braking.

According to Prevost’s published specifications, the coach has typical energy use of around 2.25 kWh per mile (1.40 kWh per kilometre), but that figure can be higher or lower depending on operating conditions.

Both Combined Charging System 1 (CCS1) and Megawatt Charging System (MCS) charging come standard. Using a CCS1 charger, the coach can charge from 20% to 80% in about 55 minutes at up to 350 kW. That drops to about 35 minutes when using MCS.

“This milestone reflects our determination to combine technological progress with the needs expressed by some of our customers,” said François Tremblay, Prevost’s president and the head of Volvo Group Canada.

While the coach was officially unveiled this week, pre-production models are already undergoing testing in Ontario and Quebec, according to Jay Menard, Prevost’s zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) programs project manager (via Electric Autonomy).

Menard said the first pilot projects are scheduled to begin in early 2027, with two more planned for the spring. Deliveries of production coaches are expected to begin by mid-August 2027.

data.title: Tesla opens new Supercharger in South Surrey
data.description:
Tesla has opened a new Supercharger in South Surrey, B.C., the eighth station for the city just south of Vancouver that is also home to one of the largest concentration of Tesla owner communities in North America.

The new Supercharger is at The Professional Centre at 3211 152 Street, where construction began in June. As of Thursday, 12 stalls are now open to Tesla and non-Tesla owners with charging speeds up to 325kW.

According to the listing, Tesla owners get the lowest price before 8 a.m., when charging costs just $0.20/kWh. The rate goes up to $0.34/kWh from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., then drops to $0.29/kWh until midnight.

The hours are the same for drivers of other EVs with an NACS adapter, who pay $0.31/kWh overnight and through the early morning, $0.53/kWh during the day, and $0.46/kWh after 8 p.m.

This new Supercharger is located just minutes away on the other side of Hwy 99 from the Supercharger at Southpoint Exchange Mall, where another 12 V2 Supercharger stalls are available for Tesla and non-Tesla drivers.

The South Surrey opening follows a busy stretch for Tesla’s charging network in B.C. In the interior of the province, Tesla opened a Supercharger in Sicamous in August and added a V4 station in Keremeos in late October. 

Northern B.C. got three new Superchargers in three days in September – Vanderhoof, Terrace and then Prince Rupert, extending Tesla’s northern charging network to the coast.

There is also another Supercharger currently under construction in Surrey near 88 Ave and Nordel Way.

data.title: Montreal plans to nearly triple daytime rates at municipal EV chargers
data.description:
Montreal is planning to significantly increase the cost of charging electric vehicles (EVs) at municipal charging stations.

The proposed increases are part of Montreal’s 2027 budget, which was presented on Tuesday and includes a balanced operating budget of $8 billion.

Under the proposed changes, EV owners who currently pay $1.10 per hour to use municipal charging stations would instead pay $3 per hour between 8 a.m. and 11:59 p.m., an increase of nearly 173%.

Charging overnight would be slightly cheaper at $2 per hour, although that still represents an increase of nearly 82% over the current hourly rate.

EV owners would also face a higher daytime rate of $4 per hour when charging is not active. The city says the changes are intended to support the continued operation of the charging network and help pay for infrastructure maintenance and renewal (via La Presse).

According to Montreal’s open data portal, there were 2,475 public EV chargers across the city as of November 1, 2026, including 2,370 Level 2 chargers and 105 direct current (DC) fast chargers.

The proposed $3 daytime rate would put municipal charging costs at the upper end of the Electric Circuit’s current hourly pricing structure for Level 2 charging stations, which allows station owners to set rates between $0.25 and $3 per hour.

According to the government, the charging rate increases would generate an additional $14 million in revenue for Montreal in 2027. However, the city’s budget still needs to be formally adopted at the end of January before it can take effect.

data.title: SpaceX Logs 56 Canadian Lobbying Reports in 2026 Despite Ottawa’s Starlink Concerns
data.description:
SpaceX has continued to engage extensively with Canadian government officials in 2026, even as Prime Minister Mark Carney has outlined plans to reduce Canada’s dependence on Starlink.

Federal lobbying records show SpaceX representatives have engaged with Canadian officials on 37 separate occasions this year, with the company and its consultants submitting a combined 56 reports to Canada’s Registry of Lobbyists.

The House of Commons and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) were the most frequently contacted institutions. SpaceX also engaged with the Prime Minister’s Office and several other federal departments.

Among those communications was an August 28 technical briefing with ISED officials, during which SpaceX submitted a 10-page assessment of how its frequency use at Janet, Alberta, and Saint-Laurent, Quebec, could affect other services.

Canada Seeks to Reduce Its Reliance on Starlink

The lobbying activity has continued since Carney’s September 23 interview with The New York Times, in which he said, “Starlink, we will diversify away from, no question.” The most recent communication recorded in the registry took place on November 13 with MP Lori Idlout and two House of Commons staff members.
